claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons have a limited magnetocaloric response under low-field cooling cycles.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons exhibit enhanced hysteresis.
Nanoscale confinement and associated residual stresses restrict a cooperative magnetostructural transition in FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons.
Heat-transfer constraints further restrict the magnetostructural transition in the low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi system.
Residual stress can pin magnetic domains and thereby increase coercivity and hysteresis losses.
Domain pinning and the restricted transition prevent the full reversible response observed in bulk material.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons likely possess fine grains and deposition-induced residual stresses.
Controlled thermal annealing can relieve residual stress in the FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
Controlled thermal annealing can promote modest grain growth without causing bulk-like coarsening.
The allowable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency is limited by substrate and film heat-transfer properties.
Dimensional confinement produces residual internal stress, small magnetic domains, and high interface density.
Annealing-induced stress reduction eases magnetic-domain-wall pinning.
Confined geometry strongly influences magnetic-domain-wall mobility in the as-deposited state.
Rapid heat transfer precludes full development of the cooperative magnetostructural transition.
Improved domain mobility and transition cooperativity decrease magnetic hysteresis.
Improved domain mobility and transition cooperativity increase the magnetocaloric temperature change.
Under identical low-field conditions, annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis-loop area than as-deposited controls.
Under identical low-field conditions, annealed samples will have a larger reversible magnetocaloric temperature change per unit field change than as-deposited controls.
The proposed behavior applies only near the expected magnetostructural-transition window and when annealing avoids phase segregation or bulk-like grain coarsening.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis, conditions, and baseline attribute the limitation to constrained or slow heat transfer, whereas the mechanism says that rapid heat transfer precludes the transition. These invoke opposite heat-transfer regimes without reconciling how each would suppress the response.
